chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Stan Getz in Horace's band before joining Benny Goodman
summary: Getz toured the Northwest in Horace's band with Crosby and Berry, a reliable reader and seller, and had to be coaxed to leave for Goodman.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Again, did you have any thoughts or feelings, because towards the end of the '40's then we had the beginning of the era of the cool music, with Miles Davis and Stan Getz. In fact, you were telling me some things about Stan Getz. He played -- he worked with you, right?

Yes, Stan Getz was a great musician. He is a great musician, I should say. I met Stan Getz out on the west coast, the far west. In fact, he made a tour up in the state of Washington, and this was just before he joined Benny Goodman. You know he played a stint with Benny Goodman. And there was always something about him that I liked. He was an excellent reader. And I had four horns. We played in San Francisco. We played in Portland, Oregon, and Seattle, Washington. I had Israel Crosby and Emmett Berry -- this was in that era -- (inaudible), and Stan was in the reed section. I had four saxophones.

And a funny thing about him, if you played two choruses that day or three, and I had a movement where the saxophones would have to come back in. He would come right back in on that note on his part, always --
He'd Stand up and play and sell, and he won an audience immediately. He never had trouble getting a gaining a

fame thing. No matter what he played, they liked it. And Benny Goodman had heard about him and had wired his mother and father about where he was and they told him, but he gave his mother and father, naturally, his itinerary with me. (Inaudible). So he got a wire from Benny Goodman, and do you know he was another guy like William Ray Nance, we had to fight him to join Benny? He was having a ball. He didn't want to leave. So finally we convinced him that this was his big break. And whatnot. (Inaudible) he joined Benny Goodman (inaudible) and made some things with him.

And he went on from there. Of course, he got a chance during later years to do his own thing. You know what happened from there on. Stan, this thing that he made was in the DownBeat, one of his solos -- da-da-da-da-da-dee-da-da, da-da-da-da --
